question: to the Commission Erik Kaliňák (NI), Judita Laššáková (NI) Subject:

In response to the results of the Hungarian elections, the President of the Commission stated on 13 April 2026 that ‘Hungary is coming back to the European path’. Nevertheless, the Commission continues to make the release of frozen EU funds conditional on the fulfilment of all 27 super milestones, with particular attention drawn to four judicial super milestones (Nos 213–216), which directly interfere with the organisation and functioning of the national judiciary-an area that, under the treaties, primarily falls within the competence of the Member States, while respecting the requirements of EU law. 1.

On the basis of which specific provision of the treaties does the Commission justify the requirements contained in super milestones 213–216, which regulate fundamental aspects of the organisation and functioning of the national judiciary (strengthening of the National Judicial Council, election of the President of the Curia, allocation of cases, preliminary references to the Court of Justice of the EU, and review of decisions by the Constitutional Court)?

How does the Commission reconcile making the release of duly allocated EU funds conditional on these requirements with the principle of the institutional autonomy of the Member States and respect for their national identity under Article 4(2) of the Treaty on European Union?

In what way does the Commission ensure that these four super milestones do not constitute a disproportionate and ultra vires interference with the constitutional order of a Member State, but remain strictly limited to the protection of the Union’s financial interests?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (15.6.2026) The Commission understands that the questions relate to Hungary’s Recovery and Resilience Plan (‘RRP’). The Recovery and Resilience Facility (‘RRF’) Regulation1 only allows disbursement of funds in case the Member State’s audit and control framework effectively protects the financial interest of the Union. In the Hungarian RRP, Hungary committed to implement in total 27 audit and control milestones (or ‘super milestones’) to ensure this. This includes four reforms to strengthen judicial independence which aims at addressing the underlying challenges identified by a dedicated country-specific recommendation on the independence of the judiciary. On 15 December 2022, the Council of the European Union approved Hungary’s RRP, including those milestones. Hungary is yet to submit a payment request. In line with the RRF legal framework, the Commission will assess the fulfilment of all milestones and targets, including the ‘super milestones’, only thereafter. As for all Member States, that assessment will be carried out in line with the applicable rules and the methodology specified in Annex I to the Communication published on 21 February 20232. In particular, the satisfactory fulfilment of milestones and targets is assessed on the basis of the criteria set out in the Council implementing decisions. In this context, the Commission has to base its assessment on the wording of each milestone and target, in light of its context and purpose, to determine whether, based on the justification provided by the Member State, those criteria are satisfactorily fulfilled or not.
